newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: The number of people filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose for the second consecutive week last week, with 6,000 more applications than the previous week, the government said on Thursday.
The Labour Department said 318,000 people filed first-time claims for unemployment insurance benefits in the week ended April 5, up from 312,000 claims in the previous week.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims at 313,000 in the April 5 week.

The rise brought the average weekly rate of new claims over the past four weeks -- a more accurate measurement of employment trends than the more-volatile weekly numbers -- to 313,500, up from 311,500 in the prior four-week period.

Total benefit rolls rose 40,000 to reach 2.308 million in the week ended March 29, the latest period for which those figures were available. That was up from 2.268 million the prior week, the department said.
Labour said nine states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended March 29, the latest period for which data were available.

They were Maryland, with 2,774 fewer claims filings; Louisiana, with 2,657; North Carolina, with 2,583; Texas, with 1,990; California, with 1,895; Kentucky, with 1,780; Michigan, with 1,753; Illinois, with 1,395; and Tennessee, with 1,361.
Maryland had fewer layoffs in the automobile and service industries. Louisiana had fewer layoffs in transportation equipment, and North Carolina had fewer layoffs in the textile industry.

Texas reported fewer layoffs in electrical equipment and trade industries. Illinois had fewer layoffs in trade, service and manufacturing industries, while Michigan had fewer layoffs in various industries throughout the state.
Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in the apparel, lumber, printing and publishing, transportation equipment and service industries. California and Kentucky had no comment.

Georgia, with 1,553 additional filings, was the only state reporting an increase in claims exceeding 1,000 in the March 29 week. The state cited more layoffs in the automobile and transportation equipment industries.
